 Election Notebook: Trenton mayoral candidate issues statement about runoff voting

 Corey McNair on Tuesday addressed members of the Mercer County Board of Elections regarding early voting.
(L.A. Parker/The Trentonian)
 By For Medianews Group PUBLISHED: November 10, 2026 at 6:54 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Editor’s Note: The Trentonian’s Election Notebook is a collection of local political announcements courtesy of the respective campaigns. To submit press releases and photos, email the editor, John Berry, at jberry@Trentonian.com 
 In the days following the election, discussions at both the city and county levels indicated that early voting would once again be made available to residents on December 4th, 5th, and 6th.
 Today, I personally attended the Board of Elections meeting at noon, expecting that a decision would be made regarding early voting. However, no decision was made. I left with the hope that the Board will carefully consider the needs of our community and ultimately make the right choice.
 Let’s be clear: This is not about Corey McNair. This is about the people of Trenton.
 We are talking about a community where many residents face everyday barriers that make exercising their right to vote difficult. We have single mothers who may not have childcare or transportation. We have seniors and residents with mobility challenges. We have working families who cannot simply walk away from their jobs to vote on one specific day. We have young people, including 18 year olds still attending high school, who may not fully understand the runoff process or realize that they must vote again. We also have formerly incarcerated individuals who recently exercised their right to vote and may not understand that they must return to the polls on December 8th.
 These are real people. These are our neighbors. And these are the very residents who could be negatively affected when voting opportunities are limited.
 I strongly believe we should be expanding opportunities for people to participate in our democracy, not making it more difficult. When we consider the socioeconomic realities of Trenton, we have to recognize that access to the ballot is not equally easy for everyone.
 I also believe there needs to be representation at the table from people who understand the realities of living in a community like Trenton. We cannot continue making decisions about our community without adequately considering the people who have to live with the consequences.
 I have serious concerns about the possibility of additional voting opportunities not being made available. I hope the Board of Elections and its legal counsel will look beyond the technicalities and consider the people behind every single ballot. Legal interpretations and statutes matter, but so does the responsibility to ensure that every eligible voter has a fair opportunity to participate.
 People marched, protested, sacrificed, and even died for the right to vote. That history should remind all of us how important it is to protect and expand access to the ballot.
 I want the residents of Trenton to understand something: Your vote on November 3rd does not automatically carry over to December 8th. This is another election, and your participation matters just as much.
 Regardless of what decision is ultimately made regarding early voting, I intend to do everything within my ability to educate, organize, and encourage our residents to show up again.
 I am hopeful that the Board of Elections will make a decision that puts the voters first. I am asking them to consider the realities of our community, listen to the concerns being raised, and make the right choice for the people of Trenton.
 This election belongs to the people of Trenton. Every eligible resident deserves a fair opportunity to participate, regardless of their circumstances, income, transportation, work schedule, or background.
 Our voices matter. Our votes matter. And I hope those making these decisions remember who they are ultimately serving: THE PEOPLE.
 — Corey Isiah McNair
